claims.head: Special teams lean toward the Oilers
claims.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.7 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Oilers’ power play is the league’s best, and the Kraken’s kill is one of the league’s worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Kraken more than most.
claims.nums: Edmonton 1st for power play (9.7 expected goals per 60) · Seattle 29th for penalty kill
claims.gist: The Oilers’ power play has a soft target in the Kraken’s kill.
claims.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 1 games this season

check.measure: expected goals per 60 on the power play
check.rule: held if tonight's figure is at or above the team's usual level; partly if between the league average and that level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: The Oilers can’t afford to cough it up
claims.call: The Kraken get at least their usual 7.5% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
claims.body: The Kraken turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Oilers are one of the league’s worst at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Oilers.
claims.nums: Seattle 10th for chances off turnovers (7.5% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Edmonton 29th for avoiding breakdowns
claims.gist: The Kraken pounce on loose pucks, and the Oilers cough them up.

claims.head: Sheltered against exposed
claims.body: The Kraken are one of the league’s best for preventing dangerous shots, at the sheltered end; the Oilers are one of the league’s worst, at the exposed end. Expect that gap to show.
claims.gist: The Kraken and the Oilers sit at opposite ends for preventing dangerous shots.
claims.call: The Kraken prevent dangerous shots better than the Oilers do.

check.rule: held if the team comes out ahead by at least half its usual margin; partly if it comes out ahead by less; otherwise didn't happen

EDM.head: Edmonton has nearly everything going for them
EDM.body: Edmonton has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Anything short of a win would be a surprise, though Seattle can make a game of it if they pounce on loose pucks.

SEA.head: Seattle has their work cut out
SEA.body: Edmonton has controlled the play far better over recent games and has home ice. Seattle’s best hope is pouncing on loose pucks, plus a big night in goal.

story.head: Draisaitl’s favourite opponent
paras: The Kraken come in at 1-0-0, the Oilers at 1-0-1.

items.text: Leon Draisaitl has a point in eight straight games against Seattle, and 19 points in his last nine against them.
Bobby McMann has six goals in seven games against Edmonton since 2023-24, most of them with Toronto.
